category_title: High-level readers receiving advanced cognitive challenges
scenario_title: Analyzing character behavior in an alternative school book
minimal_context: The student is participating in a one-on-one reading conference to discuss character behavior in a self-selected book.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's start our Phase 2 reading conference to talk about your book. Do you think he's a bad kid? Why not?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Because it really doesn't seem like he's a bad kid.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It seems like he's a shy and gentle kid and he just wants to get in to a lot of trouble to tell everybody that he's in the different school.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: ...because he's really not mean to anybody in his family, he's only mean to people in like school and the teachers.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's start our Phase 2 reading conference to talk about your book. Do you think he's a bad kid? Why not?

STUDENT: Because it really doesn't seem like he's a bad kid.

TUTOR: What else do you think?

STUDENT: It seems like he's a shy and gentle kid and he just wants to get in to a lot of trouble to tell everybody that he's in the different school.

TUTOR: Go on.

STUDENT: ...because he's really not mean to anybody in his family, he's only mean to people in like school and the teachers.

task.content: Analyzing character behavior and personality in a book about an alternative school
task.learning_goal: Determine if students are reading appropriately challenging books and to assess students’ reading readiness

context.environment: Phase 2 of the SEM-R involves individualized conferences
context.materials: Self-selected books, SEM-R bookmarks with sample higher-level and follow-up questions
context.social_setting: One-on-one reading conference with Mrs. McCarthy

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: In the book, the main character, Martin, had to go to an alternative school
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Glorimar participated in a one-on-one reading conference to talk about her self-selected book.

behavior_patterns.condition: When asked inference and justify follow-up questions within the same exchange: 'Do you think he’s a bad kid? Why not?'
